Lemma
[The inclusion of the regular part is an immersion]

↗ prop:regular-level-set-hypersurface ↗ lem:opens-inclusion-differential ↗ prop:regular-level-set-inclusion-smooth

In the setting of Proposition 5, the differential of $M_c\hookrightarrow M$ is injective at every point. Together with Lemma 5, this makes $M_c$ an embedded smooth hypersurface in $M$.

Proof

↗ lem:opens-inclusion-differential ↗ prop:regular-level-set-inclusion-smooth \sketch The chain rule factors this differential through $M_c\hookrightarrow \mathcal R$ and $\mathcal R\hookrightarrow M$. The second factor has identity differential, while the first has injective differential by Proposition prop:regular-level-set-inclusion-smooth.

□
